nodes.label: Late Growth Flock Frame (Siren, 2022-03-14 22:12:23)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren' and '2022-03-14 22:12:23' - the same calendar day as the Gas-channel frame but twelve minutes earlier. Large birds crowd the floor with only thin channels of visible litter, and dense fans of birds press against each pan feeder along the grey feed pipe.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp OSD Overlay
nodes.description: The white on-screen-display date/time string rendered by the DVR into the top-right corner of every frame (here '2022-03-14 22:12:23'). Combined with the channel name in the opposite corner it makes each exported PNG fully self-describing in time and condition.
nodes.rationale: Baking the clock into the pixels survives frame extraction, renaming and re-encoding, so temporal ordering can be recovered even when the sequential filenames (frame00001, frame00101, frame00201, frame00401) do not follow chronological order - which they demonstrably do not here. The trade-off is a permanently corrupted image region that should be cropped or masked before training.

nodes.label: Growth Progression Across the Production Cycle
nodes.description: Across the sampled dates (22 Feb, 26 Feb, 1 Mar, 14 Mar 2022) from one fixed viewpoint, mean bird size in pixels and floor coverage increase monotonically while inter-bird spacing collapses. The frame set therefore forms a longitudinal record of a single broiler production cycle rather than a set of independent scenes.
nodes.rationale: Holding the camera pose constant is what makes the comparison meaningful: because viewpoint, feeder positions and scale are unchanged, differences between frames can be attributed to the flock itself instead of to camera movement, which is what allows density and size to be read as growth indicators.
